localBiteReport: The most recent available report covering Choctawhatchee Bay inshore fishing is from the week of September 4–10, 2026 — roughly one to two weeks old. According to Capt. Blake Nelson of Last Cast Charters (reporting via the Northwest Florida Fishing Report), early fall-transition signs are appearing in Choctawhatchee Bay: water is beginning to cool, bait schools are moving from open deeper water into bayous, flats, bridge areas, and roll-downs, and redfish action on the flats is improving with sight-fishing opportunities picking up. Slot redfish, trout, and mangrove snapper have been holding around grass, sandy pockets, docks, and deeper cuts, while bull redfish and jacks have been actively feeding on pogies and greenies around Rocky Bayou, Boggy Bayou, Joe's Bayou, Marler Bayou, and the East Pass. Water temperature as of today (September 17) is 86°F. Based on seasonal patterns, the fall mullet run and a stronger slot-redfish push are expected to build from the second or third week of September into October.
